summary: The WebXR Anchors Module is a World Wide Web Consortium draft that lets a web page ask an augmented reality device to keep tracking a fixed point in the real world, so virtual objects placed there stay in place as the device's understanding of the room changes. It covers making an anchor from a pose or from a hit test result, receiving anchor updates in each frame, deleting an anchor, and a per-website handle that lets the page ask for the same anchor again in a later session. It leaves how a device actually tracks the world to the underlying system, and leaves sessions, reference spaces, units and hit testing to the core WebXR Device API and its sibling modules. A standards audience should know that the stored handles are known only to the website that made them, the device may drop them for any reason, and nothing in the text hands an anchor to another device, so it is not a shared or cloud anchor standard.

coverage.note: The module tracks poses fixed to the real world and defines no avatar mesh or appearance.

sources.title: WebXR Anchors Module (Editor's Draft, 27 April 2026), 1.1 Terminology
sources.quote: Anchor, as understood by this document, is an entity that keeps track of the pose that is fixed relative to the real world, and is created by the application.

coverage.note: The creating call names the frame its pose is expressed in by passing an XRSpace, so both sides agree on a frame for each call. There is no Earth-based or interchangeable coordinate reference system; the frames are the device-local spaces of the WebXR Device API.

sources.quote: Let anchor native origin be a new native origin returned from the device ’s call to create a new anchor using pose , interpreted as if expressed relative to effective origin at the frame ’s time .

coverage.note: Persistent handles let a website restore an anchor in a later session, but the map is stored by the device, tied to one website origin and may be pruned by the device. The text defines no way to give an anchor to another device or user.
